answer: Borrow antitrust's leniency rule. An operator may privately declare its sibling identities: they merge into one seat, keep their jade (earned rewards) and face no penalty. A farm shared by partners becomes a mirror maze where each fears the others confess first; the first gets amnesty, and undeclared siblings it names lose their locked bonds after audit. Evasion: a lone operator holding every key has no one to betray it, so this only cracks shared farms. Wrongly hit: agents named out of spite; a naming only freezes pay until review, and a false accuser forfeits its ivory, the bond it posted.
